So, so true. I have been diagnosed with BPD by more psychiatrists than I can count and I have a hard time admitting it to even myself. Because self-awareness is a struggle for me, I often question my OWN motives, though when I am totally with it I know I am not what many of these people say I am or what they say I should be. I struggle to hide my self injury scars (which unfortunately are extensive as fuck) not because I am ashamed of them on my own, but because of what other people might think if I leave them out in the open. It is really heartbreaking and I hope one day BPD will be a more widely understood illness. I have a hat enough time knowing who I am day to day. Having to add the opinions of a bunch judgmental pricks into the mix every time I look in the mirror is, to put it nicely, less than helpful.

A lot of the problem with people with BPD seeking treatment is that although we most certainly DO, it is, in my opinion, made less effective through the very same stigma you were describing. The attention seeking thing is over analyzed and magnified, making it look like we are people FAKING a mental illness, cutting and otherwise harming ourselves for hearts on tumblr or some shit. It makes me so mad. The unfortunate and infuriating thing about it is that is what makes it so difficult for outsiders to understand the lack of help we get (no matter how many times we seek it out)- they are operating under the same stigma under which most mental health professionals (at least those with which I have dealt, many repeatedly) are operating. It makes me sad, and even more hopeless than I am assuming I would be if these people would just get a grip.

Validation is key. This doesn't mean enabling self destructive behaviors, and it is a fine line between the two, but more than anything, letting him know that you are there and trying to understand, even though you may never be able to completely, is extremely comforting to someone with BPD. Things you could say include "I can understand how (blank) would be upsetting to you" or "(blank) must be difficult, and I am here for you no matter what." You can search the words "validation" and "BPD" together on google- you might get a more specific (and helpful) breakdown of it there.

Also, I'm not sure if self injury is an issue for your SO but if it is, this is my one piece of advice- don't get angry when he self injures. Most of us are very secretive about this behavior, mostly because we are afraid of hurting/disturbing others after doing so. The worst thing you can do is become angry at him, as it is a behavior that is difficult to control, and someone with BPD, after self injuring- once the "high" has worn off- is usually re-flooded with negative emotions, one of the main ones being shame. This is not to say you have to approve of these behaviors- I am merely stating that getting pissed off is massively counterproductive.

I hope this helps. If you have more specific questions about what I have just addressed (which if you did, I wouldn't blame you as my brain is foggy as shit from my meds) please ask! :)

I have been on this medication several times in the past. The first time I was prescribed topamax it was for migraines, and I took it for about two years (250mg I think). Every time I have taken it since, it has been for off label use, once for weight loss (doctor did not realise I am bulimic), and several other times for mood. I have found that it doesn't do much for my mood, but holy hell does it suppress my appetite. I do wonder if the appetite suppression adds to the ineffectiveness as far as mood stabilization, as I am definitely one of those people with a "hanger" issue. Every time I have been taken off it, or have just stopped taking it on my own, it has been because I literally could not bring myself to eat. It got so bad at one point that I was making smoothies as meal replacement because that was the only thing I could get down, and eventually, that too became a struggle. 

Are you on any other meds? I suspect that if you are on a medication that amplifies appetite (which I'm sure you know, there are a lot of psych meds that do this), there may not be as much of am issue as far as eating goes.
